# Urbo task runner. Run `just` (or `just --list`) to see all recipes.

set windows-shell := ["C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\sh.exe", "-c"]

urbo := "scripts/urbo"

# List all available recipes.
default:
    @just --list

# Bring up the whole stack for this worktree: deps, infrastructure, backend, seed data, dev servers. Flags: --fresh, --detach, --no-seed, --apps=<names>, --with-limesurvey.
up *ARGS:
    node {{urbo}}/up.mjs {{ARGS}}

# Start only the dev servers against an already-running instance (what `just up --detach` skips).
serve *ARGS:
    node {{urbo}}/serve.mjs {{ARGS}}

# Wipe this instance's data and bring everything up again from scratch.
fresh:
    node {{urbo}}/up.mjs --fresh

# Stop this instance's containers, keeping its data.
down:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs down

# Stop this instance and delete its volumes (database, search index, S3 objects).
reset:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs reset

# Re-import this instance's Keycloak realm after a template change, keeping its seeded content.
reset-auth:
    node {{urbo}}/reset-auth.mjs

# Show the status of this instance's containers.
status:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs status

# Print this instance's URLs.
urls:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs urls

# Open one of this instance's URLs in the browser. Run without a target to list them.
open target="":
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs open {{target}}

# Follow this instance's container logs. Pass a service name to narrow it down.
logs *ARGS:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs logs {{ARGS}}

# Open a shell in one of this instance's containers.
sh service:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs sh {{service}}

# List every Urbo instance running on this machine, across all worktrees.
ls:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs ls

# Remove Docker networks and volumes left behind by deleted instances.
prune:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs prune

# Run the preflight checks on their own and print how to fix what fails.
doctor:
    node {{urbo}}/preflight.mjs

# Run the unit tests for the orchestration scripts.
test-scripts:
    node --test "scripts/urbo/*.test.mjs"

# Run the Spring Boot backend on the host against this instance's infrastructure.
backend-local:
    node {{urbo}}/backend-local.mjs

# Build the citizen app and sync it into the native project, pointed at this instance.
native platform:
    node {{urbo}}/native.mjs {{platform}}

# Regenerate the aggregated CycloneDX SBOM at the repository root.
sbom:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    # The output is not committed here (see .gitignore): the nightly opencode mirror sync
    # runs this recipe and publishes the result on gitlab.opencode.de only.
    mkdir -p .sbom-tmp
    trap 'rm -rf .sbom-tmp' EXIT

    # --rerun-tasks: the CycloneDX tasks embed the checkout's git remote as the VCS
    # reference without declaring it as an input, so Gradle cannot tell that a changed
    # remote makes their output stale. A second run after `git remote set-url` would be
    # UP-TO-DATE, and a build-cache hit would replay an earlier run's remote; this flag
    # skips both the up-to-date check and the build cache. The task graph holds nothing
    # but the CycloneDX tasks (`--dry-run` lists no compile task), so it costs one
    # dependency resolution. A stale reference costs more.
    cd backend && ./gradlew --quiet --no-daemon --rerun-tasks cyclonedxBom && cd ..
    cp backend/build/reports/cyclonedx/bom.json .sbom-tmp/backend.json

    # cdxgen reads license/author/description metadata straight out of each package's
    # own files under node_modules when that tree already exists, and falls back to
    # thinner lockfile-only data when it does not -- so the same command produces a
    # materially different document depending on whether `app/` happened to be
    # installed already. `--no-install-deps` does not fix this: it only controls
    # whether cdxgen installs anything itself, not whether it reads a tree that is
    # already there. Installing here, unconditionally and from the frozen lockfile,
    # makes the output depend on pnpm-lock.yaml rather than on the caller's prior state.
    cd app && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && cd ..
    cd app && pnpm dlx @cyclonedx/cdxgen@12.8.4 --type pnpm --no-install-deps --output ../.sbom-tmp/frontend.json . && cd ..

    docker run --rm --volume "$PWD/.sbom-tmp:/work" --workdir /work \
        cyclonedx/cyclonedx-cli:0.33.1 \
        merge --input-files backend.json frontend.json --output-file merged.json

    # serialNumber, metadata.timestamp and metadata.component.bom-ref are optional in
    # CycloneDX and change on every run. cdxgen also appends a top-level `annotations`
    # entry that embeds the scan's wall-clock time in both its `timestamp` and its
    # human-readable `text` ("...created on Tuesday, September 15, 2026...") -- pure
    # generation metadata, not dependency data, so it is dropped rather than patched.
    # cdxgen additionally writes a `cdx:npm:package_json` property on local workspace
    # components whose value is the absolute filesystem path to that package's
    # package.json -- unlike the rest of `properties`, that one field is a property of
    # the checkout, not of the dependency, so it is stripped by pattern rather than by
    # name (a future generator could leak a path under a different key just as easily).
    # Stripping all of this removes what is specific to one run or one checkout --
    # timestamps, the serial number, absolute local paths -- so a rerun on the same commit,
    # the same OS and the same `origin` remote reproduces the document. Across operating
    # systems it still differs: pnpm installs optional platform dependencies only for the
    # host OS, and cdxgen reads their metadata out of node_modules. When it was generated
    # is in the mirror commit that carries it.
    #
    # Written without indentation, because the Open-Source-Software-Check skips every file
    # larger than 10 MiB before it even parses it (MAX_FILE_SIZE in
    # https://gitlab.opencode.de/DEUTSCHLAND.DIGITAL/plattform/service/automatic-evaluation/-/blob/main/src/measurements/security/software_bill_of_materials_file_exists.py).
    # Indented, this document measured 11.2 MB on 2026-09-21 and was reported as missing;
    # compact, the same content is 7.3 MB.
    node -e "const fs=require('fs');
      const bom=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('.sbom-tmp/merged.json','utf8'));
      delete bom.serialNumber;
      delete bom.annotations;
      if (bom.metadata) {
        delete bom.metadata.timestamp;
        if (bom.metadata.component) delete bom.metadata.component['bom-ref'];
      }
      const isLocalPath = (v) => typeof v === 'string' && /^\/(Users|home)\/|^\/private\//.test(v);
      for (const component of bom.components || []) {
        if (!component.properties) continue;
        component.properties = component.properties.filter((p) => !isLocalPath(p.value));
        if (component.properties.length === 0) delete component.properties;
      }
      fs.writeFileSync('sbom.cdx.json', JSON.stringify(bom) + '\n');"

# Urbo

Urbo is an open source smart city app platform that retrieves services and information from various
sources and makes them available on a single platform for citizens.

The app accesses data from city-specific backends and bundles the available content into thematic-functional
modules. Cities can configure which modules are active and adapt the branding to their own identity.

The available feature modules are:

- News
- Events
- Citizen services
- Feedback/Support
- Parking
- POIs
- Waste calendar
- Construction sites
- Funfair / Special events
- Citizen participation
- Surveys (LimeSurvey)
- Link lists
- Image spotlight
- NINA emergency alerts
- Here & Now (smart recommendations)
- Push notifications
- User account management (profile, account deletion)

Urbo is developed and maintained by [SWCode](https://swcode.io).

## Project status

Urbo is **actively developed** and in production. It runs as the citizen app of several German
cities, and development continues on `main` with releases cut from `app-v*` tags — at the time of
writing, several times per working day (278 `app-v2.0.x` releases since 2026-06-22, an average of
roughly 4-5 per working day).

- **Releases:** every release is an `app-v*` tag, listed at
  [gitlab.opencode.de/urbo-community/urbo/-/tags](https://gitlab.opencode.de/urbo-community/urbo/-/tags).
- **Versioning:** how the version numbers are formed and what a bump means is described in
  [docs/versioning.md](./docs/versioning.md).
- **Where it is going:** the feature modules listed above are the delivered scope. Planning
  happens internally at SWCode; what comes next shows up in the release tags above as it ships.
- **Contributing:** see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports go through
  [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md), not the issue tracker.

## Development

One command brings up everything for the worktree you are in — backend, CMS, citizen app and
urboards — with dependencies installed, the database seeded, and no port conflicts with any other
worktree:

```bash
just up
```

The first run asks for an instance identifier (the worktree directory name is offered as the
default) and remembers it in `.urbo-instance`. Every URL is derived from that identifier, so two
worktrees — two branches, two PRs you're reviewing side by side — can run at the same time without
touching each other's database, search index or file storage:

```
http://app.<instance>.localhost
http://cms.<instance>.localhost
http://boards.<instance>.localhost
http://api.<instance>.localhost
```

`.localhost` is the reserved TLD that every browser and OS resolves straight to `127.0.0.1` without
a DNS lookup — no `/etc/hosts` editing, no internet access needed. It also gets the frontends a
*secure context* (so `crypto.subtle` exists and Keycloak's login works): browsers grant that only to
`localhost` itself or a name ending in `.localhost`, never to a name that merely resolves to
loopback. `just urls` prints the full list (Keycloak, MeiliSearch, LocalStack, imgproxy, Mailpit, ...)
whenever you need to find them again, `just open cms` opens one straight in the browser, and
`just ls` shows every instance currently running on the machine, across all worktrees.

Start instances one at a time. Two `just up` runs beginning at the same moment are not guarded
against each other — there is no lockfile around the shared proxy setup — so a concurrent start can
race. This was judged not worth a lockfile for a local dev tool; just avoid starting two at once.

# Urbo CMS Backend

> **Start here:** `just up` from the repository root brings the whole stack up for the worktree
> you are in — this backend included, in a container, with the database seeded. You only need the
> manual steps below when you are working *on* the backend and want a Gradle restart loop, which
> is what `just backend-local` sets up for you. See
> [`scripts/urbo/services.mjs`](../scripts/urbo/services.mjs)'s header comment for how instances
> are isolated.
>
> Ports and hostnames in the sections below are the pre-instance defaults. Under `just up` every
> URL carries the instance label — `http://api.<instance>.localhost` — and only Postgres is
> published on the host, on a port `just up` prints.

Welcome to the Urbo CMS Backend! This guide will help you get started with setting up and running the application.

## Requirements

Before you begin, please ensure you have the following installed:

* [Docker](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop)
* [JDK 25](https://jdk.java.net/25/) (required only if you are not using Docker to run the Spring application.)

## Setting Up

Prerequisites: You need a personal access token to Github, either as environment variable `GITHUB_TOKEN` or as gradle
property `swcodeGprKey`. The access token is required to build the project, because it needs to pull packages from
Github.

1. Get a personal access token key on [your Github settings](https://github.com/settings/tokens).
2. Enter your secret token in as `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable.
   Alternatively, place your `swcodeGprKey=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`
   in your `%USERPROFILE%\.gradle\gradle.properties` along with your username,
   but this does not work with the docker workflow.
3. Remember to restart your terminals and all containers.

All local services are exposed via an nginx reverse proxy using `*.localhost` subdomains — under
`just up`, one per instance. No `/etc/hosts` changes are needed — `.localhost` is the reserved TLD
that every OS resolves straight to `127.0.0.1` with no DNS lookup at all, and — unlike a name that
merely resolves to loopback — it also gets the frontends a secure context, which Keycloak's login
flow needs (see `scripts/urbo/services.mjs`'s `publicHostname`).

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Backend API | http://api.\<instance>.localhost |
| Keycloak | http://keycloak.\<instance>.localhost |
| MeiliSearch | http://meilisearch.\<instance>.localhost |
| Mailpit | http://mailpit.\<instance>.localhost |
| Sendinblue Mock | http://sendinblue.\<instance>.localhost |
| LocalStack (S3) | http://localstack.\<instance>.localhost |
| imgproxy | http://imgproxy.\<instance>.localhost |
| LimeSurvey | http://limesurvey.\<instance>.localhost (opt-in, see [LimeSurvey](#limesurvey)) |
| PostgreSQL | localhost, on the port `just up` prints each run — `just status` shows it again (Postgres is the only service published on the host; everything else is reached through the proxy, above) |

`just urls` prints the rest of this list already filled in for your instance.

We have two workflows to launch the backend:

- Test workflow: Uses docker so you don't have to install JDKs to build the backend once.
- Dev workflow: Uses your local Java setup with your installed versions, built for hot reloading.

### Tester workflow

The former `spring/docker-compose.spring.yml` overlay is gone: the backend container (`spring-app`,
built from the multi-stage `Dockerfile` — no local JDK required) is now part of the main Compose
file and is started by `just up` from the repository root, image build included. The one-shot
`sample-data-loader` container it also starts waits for the backend `/health` endpoint and then
seeds demo data in three phases (push-integration content, curated categories, admin resources) —
see [Docker Sample Data](#docker-sample-data) for the full layout.

To disable sample imports for a run, `--no-seed`:

```bash
just up --no-seed
```

To rerun the sample data import after changing files in `docker/sample-data/`, from the repository
root, against an already-`up` instance:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .urbo/<instance>/env -f backend/docker/docker-compose.yml \
  --profile seed up sample-data-loader
```

### Dev workflow

`just backend-local` (see the banner at the top of this file) is the fast Gradle restart loop: it
runs `./gradlew :urbo-app:bootRun` on the host, wired to the environment `just up` already
rendered for this instance — the same Postgres, Keycloak, MeiliSearch, etc. the containerised
backend uses, with Postgres reached through its published host port. Run it against an
already-`up` instance, after stopping the containerised `spring-app` first (both would otherwise
fight over the same database and Keycloak realm) — `just backend-local` prints the exact command
for that, or run it yourself:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .urbo/<instance>/env -f backend/docker/docker-compose.yml stop spring-app
just backend-local
```

This workflow requires the correct Java version to be installed, supports the personal access
token in the gradle properties, and supports live editing without an explicit rebuild — either
from your IDE (run `io.swcode.urbo.cms.app.UrboCmsApplication`'s `main` method with the same
environment `just backend-local` sets) or via Gradle directly.

**The old manual path — `cd docker && docker compose up`, without `just` — no longer works.**
Run that way, there is no `--env-file`, so `URBO_INSTANCE` interpolates to an empty string:
`docker compose config` against the file produces broken network aliases such as
`imgproxy..internal` and `keycloak..internal`, an empty `KC_HOSTNAME`, and a realm-import mount of
`../../.urbo//imports`. Best case it stands up a rogue `docker` project with no realm; use `just up`
for the stack and `just backend-local` for the restart loop instead.

If the loader timed out before you started the local app, rerun it after the backend is up:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .urbo/<instance>/env -f backend/docker/docker-compose.yml \
  --profile seed up sample-data-loader
```

FROM amazoncorretto:25
ENV APP_NAME=urbo-cms

EXPOSE 8080

ADD https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/releases/download/v2.11.0/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar /opentelemetry-javaagent.jar

COPY urbo-app/build/libs/urbo-app.jar /app.jar

ENV SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod
ENV SERVICE_NAME=urbco-cms-backend
ENV NAMESPACE=urbo

ENV JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-javaagent:/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.resource.attributes=service.name=$SERVICE_NAME -Dotel.resource.attributes.deployment.environment=$SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE -Dotel.resource.attributes.service.namespace=$NAMESPACE"

ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app.jar"]

services:
  meilisearch:
    image: getmeili/meilisearch:v1.26.0
    environment:
      - http_proxy
      - https_proxy
      - MEILI_MASTER_KEY=${MEILI_MASTER_KEY:-masterKey}
      - MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS=${MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS:-true}
      - MEILI_ENV=${MEILI_ENV:-development}
      - MEILI_LOG_LEVEL
      - MEILI_DB_PATH=${MEILI_DB_PATH:-/data.ms}
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - meilisearch.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  urbo-backend-postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: pg_isready -U postgres
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s
    volumes:
      - ./create-databases.sh:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/create-databases.sh
      - urbo-cms-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: urbo
      POSTGRES_DB2: keycloak
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  keycloak:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.4.0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000;echo -e 'GET /health/ready HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' >&3;if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then echo 'Healthcheck Successful';exit 0;else echo 'Healthcheck Failed';exit 1;fi;"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      # A cold start does Quarkus augmentation, the Liquibase schema init and the realm import
      # before it is ready — measured at ~125s on a loaded laptop, which blew the old 30s+10x10s
      # budget by a hair. Failures during start_period do not count, and a success ends it
      # immediately, so a generous window costs a warm start nothing.
      start_period: 300s
    command: start-dev -Dkeycloak.profile.feature.upload_scripts=enabled --import-realm -Dkeycloak.migration.strategy=OVERWRITE_EXISTING
    restart: unless-stopped
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    volumes:
      - ../../.urbo/${URBO_INSTANCE}/imports:/opt/keycloak/data/import
    logging:
      driver: "json-file"
      options:
        max-size: "20m"
        max-file: "10"
    depends_on:
      mailpit:
        condition: service_started
      urbo-backend-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - keycloak.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}
    environment:
      KC_HOSTNAME: ${KC_HOSTNAME}
      KC_HOSTNAME_BACKCHANNEL_DYNAMIC: true
      KC_PROXY_HEADERS: xforwarded
      KC_DB: postgres
      KC_DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://urbo-backend-postgres:5432/keycloak?characterEncoding=UTF-8
      KC_DB_USERNAME: postgres
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN: admin
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD: admin
      KC_HEALTH_ENABLED: "true"
      KC_LOG_LEVEL: info
      KC_HTTP_ENABLED: "true"

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.29.3
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - mailpit.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  sendinblue-api:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      mailpit:
        condition: service_started
    volumes:
      - ./sendinblue:/app:ro
    command: [ "python", "/app/sendinblue_mock.py" ]
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:1080/health')" ]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s
    environment:
      PORT: 1080
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: 1025
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:

group=io.swcode.urbo
org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx1g

# Reuse task outputs across builds instead of recompiling. Without this the CI cache is
# nearly worthless: restoring ~/.gradle/caches only avoids dependency downloads, and a
# measured warm CI run still executed all 1108 tasks with 0 FROM-CACHE, coming out 277s
# SLOWER than no cache at all because the 702 MB restore cost more than it saved (#6861).
# The local cache directory lives in ~/.gradle/caches/build-cache-1, which CI already
# persists, so enabling this is what makes that cache pay for itself.
org.gradle.caching=true

  # Runs psql against the stack's existing Postgres and exits. Overriding the entrypoint keeps the
  # image's own docker-entrypoint.sh out of it, so this never starts a second Postgres server.
  limesurvey-db-init:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    profiles: ["limesurvey"]
    depends_on:
      urbo-backend-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./limesurvey/create-limesurvey-database.sh:/create-limesurvey-database.sh:ro
    entrypoint: [ "/bin/sh", "/create-limesurvey-database.sh" ]
    environment:
      PGHOST: urbo-backend-postgres
      PGPORT: "5432"
      PGDATABASE: postgres
      PGUSER: postgres
      PGPASSWORD: postgres
      LIMESURVEY_DB_NAME: limesurvey
    restart: "no"
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  limesurvey:
    image: martialblog/limesurvey:6-apache
    profiles: ["limesurvey"]
    depends_on:
      limesurvey-db-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      # A named volume, not a bind mount: Docker seeds it from the image, so LimeSurvey finds the
      # themes and generated files it ships with. A bind mount would start out empty and break it.
      - urbo-limesurvey-uploads:/var/www/html/upload
      - ./limesurvey/enable-remote-control.php:/enable-remote-control.php:ro
      - ./limesurvey/import-sample-surveys.sh:/import-sample-surveys.sh:ro
      - ./limesurvey/sample-surveys:/sample-surveys:ro
    # The image entrypoint still runs first and provisions the schema; this only replaces its
    # `apache2-foreground` command, so the API is switched on and the sample surveys are imported
    # before the site serves its first request. Separated by `;` rather than `&&` on purpose: a
    # seeding problem is a nuisance, not a reason to leave the developer without LimeSurvey at all,
    # and each script reports its own errors.
    command: [ "sh", "-c", "php /enable-remote-control.php; sh /import-sample-surveys.sh; exec apache2-foreground" ]
    environment:
      DB_TYPE: pgsql
      DB_HOST: urbo-backend-postgres
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      DB_NAME: limesurvey
      # The image defaults to this, but only as a shell variable its entrypoint never exports.
      # enable-remote-control.php needs to see the same prefix, so it is set explicitly here.
      DB_TABLE_PREFIX: lime_
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      ADMIN_USER: admin
      ADMIN_NAME: Urbo Admin
      ADMIN_EMAIL: test@test.de
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: admin
      PUBLIC_URL: ${LIMESURVEY_PUBLIC_URL}
      # No ENCRYPT_* keys on purpose. LimeSurvey then generates a throwaway security.php per
      # container, which is fine for dev: recreating the container makes previously encrypted
      # participant data unreadable, and nothing here is worth keeping.
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - limesurvey.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  sample-images:

    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro

    networks:

    labels:

# Local development only — builds the JAR inside Docker so no local JDK is required.
# Production image: ../../Dockerfile (expects a pre-built JAR from CI).
# If the base image or JVM flags in the production Dockerfile change, update this file too.

FROM eclipse-temurin:25-jdk-alpine AS build

WORKDIR /workspace/app
COPY . .
# sharing=locked: two instances building at the same time must not write this cache concurrently.
# The registry token arrives as a BuildKit secret, mounted only for this RUN: an ARG/ENV would
# persist it in the image layer, where `docker history` can read it back.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.gradle,sharing=locked \
    --mount=type=secret,id=github_token \
    chmod +x ./gradlew \
    && GITHUB_TOKEN="$(cat /run/secrets/github_token)" ./gradlew bootJar

FROM amazoncorretto:25

EXPOSE 8080

COPY --from=build /workspace/app/urbo-app/build/libs/urbo-app.jar /app.jar

ENV SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local

ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app.jar"]

          - sendinblue-api.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  localstack:
    image: gresau/localstack-persist:4
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:4566/_localstack/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 10s
    environment:
      - SERVICES=s3
      - EXTRA_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${LOCALSTACK_CORS_ORIGINS}
    volumes:
      - ./localstack:/etc/localstack/init/ready.d
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - localstack.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  imgproxy:
    image: darthsim/imgproxy:latest
    environment:
      - IMGPROXY_KEY=e4b9d1f5a2c3e6f7d8b0a9c1e3d5f7a2
      - IMGPROXY_SALT=1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d
      - IMGPROXY_SIGNATURE_SIZE=32
      - IMGPROXY_USE_S3=true
      # Bare compose service name, not the public/internal alias: this is a same-network
      # container-to-container call, exactly like spring-app's SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL below.
      - IMGPROXY_S3_ENDPOINT=http://localstack:4566
      - IMGPROXY_S3_REGION=eu-central-1
      - IMGPROXY_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true
      - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
      - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=YOUR_SECRET_KEY
      - IMGPROXY_ENABLE_DEBUG_HEADERS=true
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - imgproxy.${URBO_INSTANCE}.internal
    labels:
      io.swcode.urbo.instance: ${URBO_INSTANCE}

  spring-app:
